newsitem.title: DUBAI: Riyad Bank says agent for banks in Saudi steel Co.
newsitem.headline: Riyad Bank says agent for banks in Saudi steel Co.

text.p: Riyad bank said on Monday it had acted as agent for a group of Saudi and Gulf banks in a 1.06 billion riyal ($283 million) loan facility to Saudi Iron and Steel Company, known as Hadeed, to finance an expansion scheme.
The loan will be spent on financing "the local portion" of the hot and cold flat steel project, it said in a statement faxed to Reuters from its headquarters in the Saudi Arabian capital Riyadh.
The group includes Riyad Bank, Saudi Cairo Bank, Al Bank Al-Saudi al-Fransi and the Bahrain-based Gulf International Bank.
Hadeed said on January 7 it signed a 4.725 billion riyal loan with a consortium of local, Gulf and international banks to finance the flat steel plant.

Construction of the project began in April 1996 when Riyad Bank group arranged a 500 million riyal bridge loan facility pending the finalisation of the term of facilities, the bank added in the statement.
Hadeed is owned by industrial giant Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC).

"The Riyad Bank group is very excited about this unique opportunity to finance a major diversification milestone in the kingdom's economy in general and in its industrial sector in specific," it said. "This iron and steel complex represents the largest project of its kind in the Middle East and the Arab world".
It is expected to be completed by the second half of 1999.
Hadeed said 750 million riyals would be used to finance the construction of a new direct reduction plant that would supply the raw material -- sponge iron -- for the scheme.
This would be extended by Sumitomo Bank Ltd.
The German and Austrian government-supported export credit agencies would provide 2.268 billion riyals and international banks would provide around 647 million riyals.
Austria's Voest-Alpine industrieanlagenbau (VAI), a unit of VA Technologie AG, and Schloemann Siemag AG of Germany won SABIC's contract to build the plant.

Davy International, a unit of Trafalgar House, part of Norwegian technology and engineering group Kvaerner A/S, was awarded a $160 million contract to build the 1.1 million tonnes per year direct reduction plant last year. Trafalgar House was acquired by Norway's Kvaerner A/S in 1996.
